quote.leadership: "The key feature of this option is that the locus of decision-making control on priorities and activities is with Africa CDC and that we are fully buying into their long-term leadership, institutional capacity and networks." (D0004306.odt, Option 1 section)
quote.capacity: "PURCHASE will contribute to strengthening regional and national political and technical leadership, frameworks and capacity that facilitate a coherent, coordinated approach to supporting, embedding and sustaining evidence-informed decision making." (D0004306.odt, The way forward section)
quote.budget: "88%-£3,725,000 of the available budget to support Africa CDC to deliver the Africa CDC Health Economics Programme strategic roadmap on priority setting" (D0004306.odt, Option 1 section)

how_mechanism.q12_instrument_explanation: The programme uses a **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** with Africa CDC for the technical collaboration component (88% of budget), complemented by **strategic grant funding** for advocacy/engagement (9%) and a **competitive contract** for monitoring/evaluation (3%). The MoU enables flexible, long-term support aligned with Africa CDC’s strategic roadmap, while grants/contracts ensure accountability for specific outputs.
how_mechanism.q13_structure_description: Africa CDC acts as the **regional platform** for technical coordination, with the Africa Public Health Foundation (APHF) serving as the **intermediary grant manager** for financial administration. FCDO retains oversight but delegates day-to-day management to Africa CDC/APHF, enabling adaptive, demand-responsive support to member states.
how_mechanism.q14_selection_rationale: Africa CDC was selected due to its **political mandate from the African Union**, convening power, and existing networks (e.g., AfroHTA, Regional Collaborating Centres). The direct award aligns with FCDO’s strategic approach to back multilateral institutions with legitimacy to drive systemic change, as reflected in the multi-criteria decision analysis (scored highest for sustainability and alignment).

quote.instrument: "A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) will be signed with Africa CDC. In agreement with Africa CDC, we will seek to appoint an intermediary organisation that has an agreed arrangement with Africa CDC such as the Africa Public Health Foundation or AMREF Health Africa as the grant manager for this component." (D0004306.odt, Sourcing strategy section)
quote.selection: "Africa CDC has the political mandate from the African Union and convening power to build national ownership and can generate commitment to effective priority setting." (D0004306.odt, Option 1 section)

quote.management: "Africa CDC will be the lead strategic and technical partner, with Africa Public Health Foundation providing the required programme and financial management to enable this." (D0004306.odt, Sourcing strategy section)
quote.sub_awards: "Act as a brokering function to match scarce technical expertise with growing demand from African Union member states for capacity building and priority setting support, providing direct support or bringing in African and international partners as needed." (D0004306.odt, Option 1 section)

how_flexibility.q19_reallocation_details: Funds can be reallocated between countries/activities based on demand and windows of opportunity, as determined by Africa CDC. The programme design explicitly allows adaptation to "where our funding could deliver the greatest impact" (Option 2) or responds to "locally owned priorities and contexts" (Option 1).
how_flexibility.q20_adaptive_management_details: The programme employs an **adaptive management approach** where priorities can be adjusted based on: (1) demand from African Union member states, (2) emerging policy questions, and (3) windows of opportunity. Africa CDC retains flexibility to "adapt according to demand" (Option 1) or jointly determine focus with FCDO (Option 2).

quote.reallocation: "During this programme phase, this would be expected in 3-4 countries, but Africa CDC would have the flexibility to adapt according to demand and windows of opportunity." (D0004306.odt, Option 1 section)
quote.adaptive: "The programme adopts a patient development approach, ensuring that our offer responds to locally owned priorities and contexts and delivering as far as possible through local institutions and organisations." (D0004306.odt, Option 1 section)

how_efficiency.q22_layers_description: FCDO → Africa Public Health Foundation (intermediary grant manager) → Africa CDC (implementer). Sub-partners (e.g., AfroHTA, national institutions) are engaged directly by Africa CDC without additional layers.

quote.costs: "Overhead costs are expected to be around 8-10%, but may be permitted to be higher where these are clearly supporting regional and national institutional capacity development." (D0004306.odt, Drivers of value for money section)
quote.layers: "Led by a public health expert and with the support of Africa CDC, the Africa Public Health Foundation is well placed to provide the strategic, programme and grant management support to the Africa CDC’s Health Economics Programme in delivery of PURCHASE." (D0004306.odt, Sourcing strategy section)

q24_alternatives_considered.option: Intensive support to Africa CDC and regional networks (Option 1 - CHOSEN)
q24_alternatives_considered.description: 88% budget to Africa CDC to lead regional/national capacity building, with flexibility to adapt to demand. Focuses on institutionalizing priority-setting through Africa CDC’s mandate and networks.

q24_alternatives_considered.option: Targeted support for Africa CDC + demand-responsive national technical assistance (Option 2)
q24_alternatives_considered.description: 40% to Africa CDC for regional leadership; 48% for competitive tender to support 3-4 countries directly. FCDO retains more control over country-level activities.
88% budget for competitive tender to support up to 6 countries directly, with no regional investment. Focuses on catalyzing national capacity without regional coordination.

why_rationale.q25_why_chosen: Option 1 was selected because it: (1) **maximizes sustainability** by investing in Africa CDC’s long-term leadership and regional networks; (2) **aligns with FCDO’s strategic approach** to back multilateral institutions with political mandate; (3) **reduces management burden** by leveraging Africa CDC’s convening power; (4) **scored highest in multi-criteria analysis** (53.5 vs. 50/34.5 for other options) for delivery feasibility, strategic fit, and demand responsiveness. The choice reflects a shift toward **locally led development** and **systemic change** over project-level interventions.
q25_decision_factors: alignment with other donors (e.g., BMGF, AFD)

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Over-reliance on Africa CDC’s capacity to manage regional coordination
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Use of Africa Public Health Foundation as intermediary grant manager to provide programme/financial management support, reducing administrative burden on Africa CDC.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Fragmentation if national demands exceed regional capacity
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Africa CDC’s brokering function to match scarce expertise with demand, including bringing in African/international partners as needed.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Limited FCDO control over country-level adaptations
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Regular milestone-based oversight and alignment with Africa CDC’s continental frameworks to ensure strategic coherence.

quote.rationale: "Option 1 to fully back Africa CDC’s leadership, strengthen regional level capacity, and establish Africa CDC HEP as the coordinating institution for supporting priority setting demand and capacity at the national level has scored highest in the multi-criteria decision analysis." (D0004306.odt, Preferred option section)
quote.vfm: "Economy: Inputs for both technical collaboration and advocacy and engagement will be expected to be drawn in from locally and regionally available expertise first where possible." (D0004306.odt, Drivers of value for money section)
quote.risk: "The distinction in this option is that FCDO would retain direction and control of the focus and direction of the partnerships and activities at the country level." (D0004306.odt, Option 2 section - contrasting with Option 1’s delegation)

intersections.q27_where_constrains_who: The **African context** (weak institutional capacity, data limitations, and fiscal constraints) necessitates a **regional platform approach** (Africa CDC) rather than standalone national implementers. The document explicitly states that technical inefficiencies and scarce expertise require a **coordinated regional response** to deploy resources effectively, limiting the feasibility of purely country-level partners.
q27_constraints_detail: Technical inefficiencies in health systems (e.g., $23B lost in 2019) → Requires regional hubs to scale capacity
Data limitations for priority-setting → Needs Africa CDC’s continental frameworks/datasources
Fragmented funding streams → Demands a brokering function to match expertise with demand
Low domestic health spending → Necessitates advocacy at AU level (e.g., Abuja target)
intersections.q28_what_determines_how: The **need for sustained priority-setting capacity** (a continuous task, not one-off) shapes the **long-term partnership modality** with Africa CDC. The **dual focus on political commitment + technical capacity** drives the mixed structure: (1) **advocacy/engagement** (9% budget) to generate demand, and (2) **technical collaboration** (88% budget) to supply frameworks/tools. The **regional scale** of the problem (54 countries with UHC gaps) necessitates a **platform model** (Africa CDC) over bilateral projects.
q28_linkages: Objective: Institutionalize priority-setting → Mechanism: MoU with Africa CDC (long-term, flexible)
Objective: Strengthen regional leadership → Mechanism: Regional hubs (West/East Africa) + AfroHTA network
Objective: Respond to country demand → Mechanism: Africa CDC’s brokering function for technical support
Objective: Equity in access → Mechanism: Participatory priority-setting processes with marginalized groups
intersections.q29_equity_vs_efficiency_tradeoffs: The document explicitly discusses tensions between: (1) **speed vs. inclusion**: Rapid scaling of priority-setting frameworks must balance with "deliberative processes that bring in subjective views from communities" (equity); (2) **regional coordination vs. national adaptation**: Africa CDC’s continental frameworks aim for efficiency but must adapt to "locally owned priorities" (equity); (3) **technical expertise vs. ownership**: International partners (e.g., NICE) provide scarce expertise, but capacity must be institutionalized in African entities for sustainability.

q29_tradeoffs_detail.detail: Efficiency gains from regional frameworks (e.g., AfroHTA) must incorporate "participatory approaches as guiding principles" to avoid excluding vulnerable groups.
International technical support (e.g., iDSI, NICE) is used as a "complement" to African leadership, with explicit institutionalization goals (e.g., ACEPS in Ethiopia).
Regional hubs (West/East Africa) enable spillover benefits but may limit intensive support to fewer countries (3-4 direct vs. 6 in Option 3).

intersections.risk_affects_management: The **moderate risk profile** (institutional gaps, not conflict) justifies **milestone-based oversight** rather than intensive management. FCDO delegates day-to-day delivery to Africa CDC/APHF but retains strategic alignment through the MoU’s frameworks.
intersections.capacity_shapes_roles: The **capacity-building core objective** shapes partner roles by: (1) Positioning Africa CDC as the **technical leader** (not just a grantee); (2) Using APHF as a **grant manager** to free Africa CDC for strategic functions; (3) Engaging national institutions (e.g., KEMRI) as **implementation partners** with mentorship from regional networks (e.g., AfroHTA).

quote.equity: "Equity will be assessed through the extent to which the voices of vulnerable and marginalised groups are incorporated into priority setting processes and decisions." (D0004306.odt, Value for money section)
quote.capacity: "PURCHASE will first and foremost centre on reinforcing country and regional leadership, priorities and capacity, drawing in collaborative partnerships including with UK institutions and other partners to support capacity building where this is sought and needed by local partners." (D0004306.odt, The way forward section)

key_programme_risks.risk: Insufficient political commitment to UHC at national level
Limited technical capacity for priority-setting in countries
Fragmentation of efforts without regional coordination
Over-reliance on external expertise without local institutionalization
Data limitations hindering evidence-based decisions
Safeguarding vulnerabilities in participatory processes
Financial mismanagement or corruption in health systems

risk_mitigation_pairs.mitigation: Advocacy component (9% budget) to engage decision-makers; leverage Africa CDC’s AU mandate for high-level buy-in.
Africa CDC’s brokering function to deploy scarce expertise; institutionalize capacity through regional hubs (e.g., AfroHTA).
Continental frameworks and regional hubs (West/East Africa) to coordinate support.
Explicit focus on institutionalizing capacity in African entities (e.g., ACEPS, HEPU); peer-to-peer learning networks.
Develop context-relevant data sources through Africa CDC’s Health Economics Programme.
Adherence to FCDO safeguarding standards; participatory approaches designed to include marginalized groups.
Intermediary grant manager (APHF) for fiduciary oversight; milestone-based payments.

fcas_specific_lessons: Lessons from previous health financing programmes (e.g., MCHSS) highlight the need for **long-term institutional support** rather than time-bound projects.
The **Abuja target** (15% government spending on health) demonstrates that political commitments require **sustained advocacy and technical backing** to translate into action.
Regional platforms (e.g., SPARC) show that **peer learning networks** can catalyze systemic improvements in FCAS contexts by sharing adaptive solutions.
risks_lessons.lessons_from_previous: The **MCHSS evaluation (2020)** recommended that future support for health technology assessments should focus on **building long-term institutions**, as priority-setting is a continuous task. This lesson directly shaped PURCHASE’s design to reinforce **regional leadership** (Africa CDC) and **institutional capacity** (e.g., AfroHTA) rather than ad-hoc technical assistance.
design_changes_based_on_learning: Shift from **project-based** to **institutional support** (e.g., Africa CDC Health Economics Programme as a permanent structure).
Inclusion of **regional hubs** (West/East Africa) to address the **scaling challenge** identified in MCHSS.
Explicit **adaptive management** clauses to respond to demand windows, addressing MCHSS’s rigidity critique.
Stronger **equity focus** in priority-setting processes, incorporating lessons on marginalized groups’ exclusion from previous programmes.

quote.lessons: "The MCHSS evaluation recommended that future support to health technology assessments – a key to line evidence-informed priority setting approaches – should continue to build long-term institutions as priority setting is a constant task, not a one-off activity." (D0004306.odt, The way forward section)
quote.design: "PURCHASE will first and foremost centre on reinforcing country and regional leadership, priorities and capacity, drawing in collaborative partnerships... to support capacity building where this is sought and needed by local partners." (D0004306.odt, The way forward section)

financial_details.leverage_achieved: The programme aligns with and leverages existing investments by BMGF, AFD, and the World Bank in Africa CDC’s Health Economics Programme, enabling **coordinated resource allocation** and **shared overhead costs**. The regional platform approach is expected to catalyze additional funding from African Union member states by demonstrating the value of priority-setting.

quote.budget: "Programme Value: Up to £4.25m" (D0004306.odt, Summary Sheet section)
quote.breakdown: "Overhead costs are expected to be around 8-10%, but may be permitted to be higher where these are clearly supporting regional and national institutional capacity development." (D0004306.odt, Drivers of value for money section)
quote.leverage: "Programmatically, aligning our funding alongside other donors such as the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, Agence Française de Développement and the World Bank in supporting the Africa CDC as an institution and enabling Africa CDC Health Economics Programme to lead the decision-making on how best to use this funding contributes to a more efficient allocation and coordination of development partner resources." (D0004306.odt, Value for money section)

metadata.programme_name: WASH Systems for Health
metadata.quote: "The programme will contribute to better health, nutrition and education, especially for poorer households and communities, and for women and girls in particular." (D0007594.odt, Summary Information)
metadata.duration_source: "Original project start and end dates: 27/02/2024–30/03/2028" (D0007594.odt, Summary Information) and "Implementation will be programmed over the following four years, ensuring there is sufficient time to embed change." (D0003087.odt, Summary)

what_objectives.q1_explanation: The programme focuses on **systems strengthening** (capacity building) to improve WASH services, while also aiming to **unlock finance** (financing mechanism) and **generate evidence** (implementation research) for global WASH sector learning. It directly supports service sustainability but does not deliver services itself.
what_objectives.q1_source: "WASH Systems for Health will support governments in up to five developing countries in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia to strengthen the systems needed to establish reliable, resilient and inclusive WASH services over five years." (D0003087.odt, Summary) AND "The programme’s influence extends well beyond five priority countries... by establishing a global WASH systems support hub which responds to demand from governments and Posts for advice and support on WASH systems strengthening." (D0003087.odt, Summary)

q3_expected_outputs.output: WASH systems strengthened in up to 8 countries (originally 5, expanded to 6 + 2 fragile contexts)
q3_expected_outputs.quantitative: 8 countries total

q3_expected_outputs.output: Specific advice on WASH systems strengthening provided to ODA-eligible governments via a global WASH systems hub
Lessons and good practices shared globally through networks/channels
Increased use of inclusive, reliable, and resilient WASH services (Outcome 1)
Development organisations use evidence generated by the programme to inform WASH systems strengthening (Outcome 2)
Progressive reduction in preventable deaths of mothers, children, and infants caused by WASH-related infections (Impact)
Strengthened capacity and resilience of WASH sector in fragile, conflict, and violence-affected contexts (new output for FCAS expansion)
Early warning/early action systems developed in Madagascar (FCAS component)
Climate-resilient safely managed sanitation action plan for Madagascar
WASH finance strategy and climate finance proposals for Madagascar
q3_expected_outputs.quantitative: 1 Concept Note for climate finance funding

q3_expected_outputs.output: Support for South Sudan’s Presidential WASH Compact priorities
Updated national WASH information management system in South Sudan

what_objectives.summary: The programme shifts FCDO’s WASH approach from project-based service delivery to **systems strengthening**, aiming to make WASH services sustainable, climate-resilient, and inclusive. It combines **direct technical assistance** to governments, **evidence generation** for global learning, and **finance mobilization** to accelerate SDG6 progress, with a focus on women/girls and fragile contexts.
what_objectives.quote: "The programme’s focus on systems marks a fundamental shift in FCDO’s approach to WASH... ensuring that women are empowered to take informed decisions about the services they receive; and it will attract new public and private finance to accelerate progress towards SDG6 WASH targets." (D0003087.odt, Summary)

where_context.q5_risk_evidence: The programme explicitly targets **fragile and conflict-affected states (FCAS)** like South Sudan and Madagascar, where systems challenges are compounded by conflict, climate vulnerability, and weak governance. The addendum highlights that FCAS require adapted approaches to work across the humanitarian-development-peace nexus.
where_context.q5_source: "Fragile and Conflict-Affected States (FCAS) are within scope of the programme’s purpose, but the approach to working in contexts with higher, or multiple degrees fragility or conflict has specific sets of systems challenges." (D0007594.odt, Summary Information) AND "The programme has a moderate residual risk rating. Key residual risks... concern delivery, finance and context." (D0003087.odt, Risk Section)
where_context.q6_constraints_impact: Fragile contexts require **adapted systems approaches** that reinforce (rather than substitute) local capacity, link governance with service providers, and navigate **political economy barriers**. Climate risks (e.g., droughts, cyclones in Madagascar) and **limited government financial resources** further constrain service sustainability. The humanitarian-development nexus adds complexity to coordination and financing.
where_context.quote: "In fragile settings, the approach needs to be adapted, with more emphasis on resilience and localised interventions that reinforce rather than substitute pre-existing capacity and systems." (D0003087.odt, Lessons Learned) AND "The assessments also highlighted the need for a partner to be able to work across the humanitarian, development and peace nexus." (D0007594.odt, Approach to Implementation)

who_partners.lead_institution_name: FCDO (funding/oversight) with UNICEF (FCAS implementation) and NGO consortia (stable countries)
who_partners.q9_north_south_decision_power: The programme is **jointly designed** with governments (South) and implemented by a mix of **Southern-based NGOs** (e.g., in-country partners) and **multilateral/UK-managed entities** (e.g., UNICEF, FCDO). Decision-making for country-level interventions involves **host governments and Posts**, with FCDO providing strategic oversight. UNICEF’s role in FCAS leverages its **local government access** and **global climate finance accreditation** (e.g., Green Climate Fund).
q10_capacity_building_details: technical assistance to governments on WASH systems governance
training on solar-powered water systems (Madagascar)
support for developing climate finance proposals
strengthening WASH information management systems (South Sudan)
mentorship for humanitarian-development nexus coordination
institutional strengthening of service authorities (e.g., water utilities, local government branches)

partner_organizations.role: Implementation partner for FCAS (Madagascar, South Sudan, + reserve countries); climate resilience and humanitarian-development nexus expertise

partner_organizations.name: IRC WASH
partner_organizations.role: Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) partner; learning capture and global knowledge sharing

partner_organizations.name: National Governments
partner_organizations.role: Primary beneficiaries and co-implementers; responsible for executing joint action plans with FCDO support

partner_organizations.name: Local NGOs/Social Enterprises
