who_partners.quote: "UNICEF is the global lead on humanitarian WASH interventions... has extensive access to key government representatives at national and sub-national level... and is accredited to the Green Climate Fund." (D0007594.odt, Approach to Implementation) AND "Implementing partners would be procured through an appropriate mechanism such as a commercial contractor or accountable grant (AG)." (D0003087.odt, Option 2)

how_mechanism.q12_instrument_explanation: The programme uses a combination of **accountable grants (AGs)** for NGOs, **commercial contracts** for technical assistance, and **direct funding to multilateral partners (UNICEF)**. Payments are linked to **verified results** (e.g., KPIs for service sustainability) and include **performance-based incentives** for professionalized service delivery models (e.g., Uptime).
how_mechanism.q13_structure_description: FCDO **manages the overall programme** with support from a **central team** (SRO, technical adviser) and **country Posts**. Implementation is decentralized: **UNICEF leads in FCAS**, while **NGO consortia** (selected via accountable grants/contracts) operate in stable countries. A **global WASH systems hub** responds to ad-hoc demand from non-intervention countries. Monitoring is conducted by **IRC WASH**, with **quarterly reviews** and **annual independent assessments**.
how_mechanism.q14_selection_rationale: UNICEF was **directly selected** for FCAS due to its **unique humanitarian-development nexus expertise** and **Green Climate Fund accreditation**. For stable countries, partners were chosen via a **restricted competition** (accountable grants/contracts) based on **technical capacity** and **alignment with FCDO’s systems-strengthening approach**. The Uptime model (Option 1) was considered for its **proven sustainability** (90%+ functionality rates) but required government readiness.
how_mechanism.quote: "UNICEF approached FCDO with a concept note... Given its comparative advantage across the humanitarian, development peace nexus and its leadership on climate-resilient WASH services, UNICEF would be the preferred delivery partner for this work in FCAS." (D0007594.odt, Approach to Implementation) AND "Implementing partners would be procured through an appropriate mechanism such as a commercial contractor or accountable grant (AG)." (D0003087.odt, Option 2)

how_governance.q17_governance_details: The programme is overseen by **FCDO’s central team** (with input from Posts) and a **technical advisory mechanism** (e.g., IRC WASH for MEL). UNICEF’s FCAS work is governed through **joint action plans** with host governments, while NGO implementations follow **FCDO-approved results frameworks**. A **WASH systems hub** provides on-demand support to non-intervention countries, with **quarterly progress reviews** and **annual independent verifications**.
how_governance.quote: "We will monitor implementation through 6-monthly narrative and financial reports. Quarterly meetings with the headquarters, regional and country teams... will provide updates on progress, risks and opportunities." (D0007594.odt, Programme Management) AND "Progress would be independently verified using the results matrix." (D0003087.odt, Option 2)

how_flexibility.q19_reallocation_details: Funds can be **reallocated between countries** (e.g., reserve country for Yemen/DRC) or **components** (e.g., £0.5m unallocated for FCAS learning/emergency response), but requires **FCDO approval**. The **annual review process** allows adjustments based on political/economic changes.
how_flexibility.q20_adaptive_management_details: The programme uses an **adaptive approach** with **annual reviews** to refine the theory of change. **Phased interventions** (e.g., addressing bottlenecks sequentially) and **real-time monitoring** (e.g., smart technology for water services) enable responsiveness. UNICEF’s FCAS work includes **contingency planning** for shocks.
how_flexibility.quote: "Annual Reviews should review and refine the theory of change. Plans should not over-assume government interest or capacity to deliver but focus on identifying and clearing key bottlenecks." (D0003087.odt, Risk Section) AND "The additional work delivered under this programme will strongly support our WASH policy and engagement on the global stage." (D0007594.odt, Programme Management)

how_efficiency.q22_layers_description: FCDO → **Implementing Partners (UNICEF/NGOs)** → **Sub-national Service Providers/Government Agencies** (e.g., water utilities, local authorities). For Uptime-like models: FCDO → **UCF (fund manager)** → **Social Enterprises** → **Community Operators**.
how_efficiency.quote: "Consortium partners are paid by UCF in arrears against a set of independently verified KPIs." (D0003087.odt, Option 1) AND "The proposed £1.3m project budget could support work in up to five countries—demonstrating the concept to government and other development partners." (D0003087.odt, Option 1)

q24_alternatives_considered.description: Business-as-usual approach focusing on **direct WASH service provision** (e.g., infrastructure) with limited systems strengthening, based on FCDO’s previous WASH Results Programme. Estimated to reach fewer countries (2-3) with £18.5m.
Incentivizing **private/social enterprise operators** to achieve sustainability KPIs (e.g., Uptime model). Requires government readiness to outsource O&M and provide subsidies (~$0.5/person/year).

Comprehensive **systems strengthening** via technical assistance, capacity building, and governance reforms. Includes a **global WASH systems hub** for demand-driven support. Selected for its **scalability** and **alignment with SDG6**.
Focused on **mobilizing climate/private finance** for WASH (e.g., via Resilient Water Accelerator). Complementary to Option 2 but narrower in scope.

why_rationale.q25_why_chosen: Option 2 (Addressing Systemic Bottlenecks) was selected because it: 1) **Aligns with FCDO’s strategic shift** from projects to systems; 2) Offers **scalability** (global hub + multi-country reach); 3) Addresses **root causes** of poor WASH sustainability (e.g., weak governance, finance gaps); 4) Enables **adaptive learning** via the WASH systems hub; and 5) **Leverages UK comparative advantage** in systems thinking (e.g., political economy analysis, digital tools). The **FCAS expansion** (via UNICEF) was added to test resilience approaches in high-risk contexts.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Host governments fail to own reforms
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Prioritize countries with **demonstrated demand** from Posts/governments; use **political economy analysis** to tailor interventions; embed **diplomatic influence** via Posts.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Insufficient funds/time for meaningful change
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Phase interventions; focus on **key bottlenecks**; use **adaptive management** to reprioritize annually.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Stakeholders fail to collaborate
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Establish **joint action plans** with governments; leverage **multi-stakeholder platforms** (e.g., Sanitation and Water for All).

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Users unable/unwilling to pay for services
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Design **affordable tariffs** with subsidies for poorest; test **payment-by-results** models (e.g., Uptime).

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Investors avoid WASH sector
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Develop **bankable projects** (e.g., climate finance proposals); partner with **Resilient Water Accelerator** to de-risk investments.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: FCAS volatility disrupts delivery
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Use **UNICEF’s nexus expertise**; build **contingency funds** (£0.5m reserve); focus on **resilience-building** (e.g., early warning systems).

why_rationale.quote: "Success is contingent on securing and maintaining government ownership... We will only work in countries where there is strong demand from Posts to be associated with this programme." (D0003087.odt, Risk Section) AND "UNICEF’s intervention is designed to deliver value for money for the UK. It builds on existing work in Madagascar and leverages approximately £236,000 of funds to support water resource assessments." (D0007594.odt, Summary Information)

intersections.q27_where_constrains_who: The **FCAS context** limits partners to those with **humanitarian-development nexus experience** (e.g., UNICEF) and **local government access**. Stable countries allow for **NGO/social enterprise models** (e.g., Uptime), while fragile states require **multilateral actors** with risk tolerance. Climate vulnerability further narrows partners to those with **climate finance accreditation** (e.g., UNICEF’s Green Climate Fund status).
q27_constraints_detail: FCAS requires partners with **nexus capabilities** (humanitarian-development-peace)
Climate-resilient WASH needs **accredited climate finance partners**
Weak institutions limit reliance on **local NGOs alone** (need multilateral backup)
Conflict zones exclude **purely development-focused actors**
intersections.q28_what_determines_how: The **systems-strengthening objective** drives the **decentralized, adaptive structure**: 1) **Multi-country scope** → needs **global hub** for cross-learning; 2) **Focus on governance/finance bottlenecks** → requires **technical assistance contracts** (not just grants); 3) **FCAS inclusion** → mandates **UNICEF’s nexus model**; 4) **Climate resilience** → adds **finance mobilization** (e.g., GCF proposals) to delivery.
q28_linkages: Systems focus → **open partnership structure** (hub + multiple implementers)
FCAS goals → **UNICEF’s nexus role** (vs. NGOs in stable countries)
Evidence generation → **embedded MEL partner (IRC WASH)**
Finance mobilization → **performance-based contracts** (e.g., Uptime KPIs)
intersections.q29_equity_vs_efficiency_tradeoffs: The programme explicitly balances **equity** (e.g., targeting women/girls, poor households, FCAS) with **efficiency** (e.g., phased bottlenecks approach, leveraging existing systems). Trade-offs include: 1) **FCAS adaptation** (higher costs for resilience) vs. **scale in stable countries**; 2) **Local ownership** (slow, capacity-dependent) vs. **multilateral speed** (UNICEF); 3) **Inclusive design** (e.g., gender/disability) adding complexity to **standardized delivery**.

q29_tradeoffs_detail.detail: South Sudan/Madagascar interventions are **higher-cost** (e.g., early warning systems) but reach **vulnerable populations**, while stable countries allow **standardized models** (e.g., Uptime).
Government-led reforms are **slower** but sustainable, while UNICEF’s **pre-existing systems** enable faster delivery in FCAS.
Gender/disability inclusion (e.g., menstrual hygiene facilities) adds **design complexity** but aligns with **SDG5/10**.
Annual reprioritization allows **responsiveness** but reduces **long-term planning certainty** for partners.

intersections.risk_affects_management: High-risk FCAS contexts (e.g., South Sudan) receive **intensive oversight** (quarterly reviews + embedded advisors), while stable countries (e.g., Malawi) use **lighter-touch milestone checks**. The **£0.5m contingency fund** and **reserve country** (Yemen/DRC) reflect **risk-based flexibility**.
intersections.capacity_shapes_roles: Partners’ capacities dictate roles: 1) **UNICEF** handles FCAS due to **nexus expertise**; 2) **NGOs/social enterprises** (e.g., Uptime) operate in stable contexts with **technical O&M skills**; 3) **IRC WASH** leads MEL based on **global learning mandate**; 4) **Governments** co-design interventions based on **institutional readiness** (e.g., tariff reforms).
intersections.quote: "The approach to working in contexts with higher, or multiple degrees fragility or conflict has specific sets of systems challenges... It requires partner organisations to have the experience and capability in those countries, and to work across the humanitarian and development nexus." (D0007594.odt, Summary Information) AND "A phased approach reflects WHO recommendations for Health Systems Strengthening... Political will to introduce and drive reform is a prerequisite for systems strengthening." (D0003087.odt, Lessons Learned)

key_programme_risks: Host governments fail to sustain reforms (e.g., tariff policies, subsidies)
Insufficient UK funds/time to implement planned interventions
Interventions lack depth/scale to drive measurable change
Stakeholders (e.g., private sector, other donors) fail to collaborate
Users unable/unwilling to pay for improved services
Investors avoid WASH sector despite de-risking efforts
FCAS volatility (conflict, climate shocks) disrupts delivery
Weak local capacity undermines system changes post-programme
Climate change exacerbates water scarcity/service failures
Political transitions derail reform momentum

risk_mitigation_pairs.mitigation: Select countries with **Post demand** and **political will**; use **diplomatic influence**; co-develop **joint action plans**.
Phase interventions; focus on **key bottlenecks**; reprioritize via **annual reviews**.
Leverage **multi-stakeholder platforms** (e.g., SWA); align with **other FCDO programmes** (e.g., EPD Centre).
Design **affordable tariffs** + **targeted subsidies**; test **payment-by-results** (e.g., Uptime).
Develop **bankable projects** (e.g., climate finance proposals); partner with **Resilient Water Accelerator**.
Use **UNICEF’s nexus expertise**; allocate **£0.5m contingency**; focus on **resilience** (e.g., early warning systems).
Embed **long-term TA**; strengthen **local service providers** (e.g., utilities, social enterprises).

fcas_specific_lessons: Link **local governance** (administrative/traditional) with **service providers** and **user groups**
Ensure humanitarian interventions **reinforce (not substitute)** local systems
Prioritize **preparedness** (e.g., early warning systems) over reactive responses
Use **market actors/supply chains** to fill gaps in state capacity
Adapt **financial models** (e.g., subsidies) for affordability in crises
risks_lessons.lessons_from_previous: Past FCDO WASH programmes (e.g., WASH Results) showed **limited sustainability** (53% water supplies functional post-project) due to **weak O&M systems** and **community-based management failures**. Successful models (e.g., Uptime) used **professionalized operators** with **performance-based funding** (90%+ functionality). **Political leadership** (e.g., India’s Swachh Bharat) was critical for scale. **Phased reforms** (incremental steps) and **donor coordination** improved outcomes.
risks_lessons.design_changes_based_on_learning: 1) Shifted from **project-based delivery** to **systems strengthening**; 2) Added **FCAS component** (UNICEF) based on Post demand; 3) Integrated **climate resilience** (e.g., solar water systems, GCF proposals); 4) Expanded **global hub** for cross-learning; 5) Included **adaptive management** (annual reviews, contingency funds).
risks_lessons.quote: "A recent FCDO assessment of the sustainability of WASH services... found that only 53% of water supplies continued to provide a reliable service and 66% of household toilets... remained functional." (D0003087.odt, Evidence) AND "The assessments also highlighted the need for a partner to be able to work across the humanitarian, development and peace nexus." (D0007594.odt, Approach to Implementation)

financial_details.leverage_achieved: UNICEF’s work aims to mobilize **climate finance** (e.g., Green Climate Fund proposals) and **private investment** via the Resilient Water Accelerator. Previous UNICEF-led proposals under GWL generated **$350m in potential climate finance**, benefiting up to 9 million people.
financial_details.capital_vs_revenue_split: Budget includes **capital expenditures** (e.g., rehabilitating water infrastructure in Uptime model) and **revenue support** (e.g., subsidies for O&M, TA for governance reforms). FCAS component focuses on **systems/software** (e.g., early warning systems) over hardware.
financial_details.quote: "UNICEF’s intervention is designed to deliver value for money for the UK. It builds on existing work in Madagascar and leverages approximately £236,000 of funds to support the water resource assessments." (D0007594.odt, Summary Information) AND "An estimated 30% of programme spend will be eligible as ICF spend under ICF Key Performance Indicator (KPI15)." (D0003087.odt, Climate Section)

metadata.programme_name: HealthSystemsConnect: Connecting UK experts with partner countries to enhance health diplomacy and strengthen health systems for all

quote.programme_name: "HealthSystemsConnect: Connecting UK experts with partner countries to enhance health diplomacy and strengthen health systems for all." (D0003600.odt, Title section)
quote.duration: "The budget for this programme is up to £2.93m of ODA, RDEL over three years" (D0003600.odt, Financial Details section)
quote.start_year: "Date of Approval of Business Case: 06/04/2023" (D0003600.odt, Summary Sheet section)

metadata.duration_source: "The budget for this programme is up to £2.93m of ODA, RDEL over three years"

what_objectives.q1_explanation: The programme primarily focuses on **capacity building** (strengthening health systems in partner countries) and **policy influence** (enhancing UK health diplomacy and supporting UHC goals). It also includes elements of **implementation research** (testing partnership models) and **service delivery** (technical exchanges). The core is a **technical partnership** approach to co-develop health system solutions.
what_objectives.q1_source: "Building upon the global brand of the NHS and the UK’s global reputation in health systems strengthening, this programme will provide posts and host governments with access to British health expertise through technical exchange with experts working across the UK’s health policy, planning and delivery ecosystem... to achieve universal health coverage by 2030." (D0003600.odt, Programme Summary)

q3_expected_outputs.output: UK-host country strategic health partnerships formed/strengthened
self-sustaining multi-stakeholder knowledge-sharing networks
enhanced health system capabilities in partner countries
co-produced health policies, strategies, and tools
multi-country learning exchanges
delegation visits to the UK (4 visits/year in Years 2-3)
q3_expected_outputs.target: 4 visits per year

q3_expected_outputs.output: NHS technical draw-down days
q3_expected_outputs.target: 250 days (Year 1), 350 days (Year 2), 300 days (Year 3)

q3_expected_outputs.output: stronger evidence base for system-to-system health partnerships

what_objectives.summary: The programme aims to leverage UK NHS expertise to strengthen health systems in ODA-eligible countries through demand-responsive technical partnerships, knowledge exchange, and policy influence, contributing to Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by 2030. It operates as a 'one-stop shop' (NHS Consortium for Global Health) to facilitate access to UK health expertise.

quote.objectives: "The programme contributes to several priorities across the International Development Strategy, Integrated Review, forthcoming Global Health Strategic Framework... Its aim to provide demand-responsive British expertise delivers UK commitments to take a health systems strengthening approach to increasing access to vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics... reducing the risk of future health threats including climate change and ending the preventable deaths of mothers, babies and children." (D0003600.odt, Rationale for UK Aid Spending)
quote.approach: "The programme’s model of demand-driven technical partnership and mutually beneficial knowledge exchange is aligned to the growing calls to move beyond historic aid dynamics... and work in partnership with countries to share skills and co-develop solutions." (D0003600.odt, Strategic Case)

countries_regions: Potential focus: Philippines, South Africa, FCDO Ending Preventable Deaths (EPD) Flagship countries, middle-ground powers
where_context.q5_risk_evidence: The programme is rated as 'moderate risk' based on FCDO risk appetite and experience from the predecessor Better Health Programme. Risks include political context changes, demand outstripping capacity, and budget uncertainty, but robust governance and flexibility are built in.
where_context.q5_source: "The overall risk rating for the programme is considered as moderate (see Management Case)." (D0003600.odt, Risk Management)
q6_contextual_constraints: technical capacity (limited NHS/ALB resources vs. demand)
reputational risks (NHS domestic pressures affecting global credibility)
where_context.q6_constraints_impact: Political changes or ODA budget reductions could limit programme scope or force re-scoping. High demand for NHS expertise may outstrip available technical resources, requiring prioritization. Reputational risks could undermine UK influence if NHS domestic challenges affect its global standing.

quote.risk: "Risk that FCDO centralised funding may be reduced year-on-year due to competing FCDO priorities... impacting programme delivery and outcomes and impacting sustainability of interventions." (D0003600.odt, Risk Table)
quote.constraints: "Risk that FCDO network demand outstrips the available technical resource." (D0003600.odt, Risk Table)

who_partners.q9_north_south_decision_power: The NHSC (UK-based) triages requests, matches technical experts, and quality-assures interventions. FCDO Posts commission assignments, but the NHSC controls the technical draw-down mechanism and knowledge brokering. Partner countries can request support but do not lead the platform.
q10_capacity_building_details: peer-to-peer learning networks
technical exchanges with UK experts
delegation visits to UK health institutions
co-development of health policies/tools
skills transfer through joint interventions

partner_organizations.name: NHS Consortium for Global Health (NHSC)
partner_organizations.role: Lead implementing platform; coordinates technical draw-down, knowledge brokering, and programme management

partner_organizations.name: NHS England (NHSE) and UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA)
partner_organizations.role: Co-hosts of NHSC; provide governance and technical oversight

partner_organizations.name: NHS Arm’s Length Bodies (ALBs)
partner_organizations.role: Provide technical expertise (e.g., NICE, CQC, Health Education England, Public Health Wales)

partner_organizations.name: FCDO Posts (country offices)
partner_organizations.role: Commission technical assignments, facilitate country-level influencing, and quality-assure interventions

partner_organizations.name: Ministries of Health (partner countries)
partner_organizations.role: Request technical support, co-develop solutions, and participate in learning networks

partner_organizations.name: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) International
partner_organizations.role: Strategic oversight via Programme Strategic Advisory Board

partner_organizations.name: Department for Business and Trade (DBT)
partner_organizations.role: Representation on Strategic Advisory Board; potential commercial linkages

partner_organizations.name: External Evaluation Provider (TBD)
partner_organizations.role: Independent evaluation to build evidence on partnership effectiveness

quote.structure: "Working through the NHSC this programme will complement wider in-country health investments... providing coordinated not-for-profit access to a range of technical specialists from across the NHS and UK health sector." (D0003600.odt, Strategic Case)
quote.decision_power: "NHSC will provide input to quality assurance processes, including via six-monthly reporting and annual reviews... FCDO Post commissioning lead will facilitate country-level influencing... and report into programme governance." (D0003600.odt, Management Case)

how_mechanism.q12_instrument_explanation: The programme is governed by a **non-legally binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** between FCDO and NHSC. The MoU outlines payment terms, performance expectations, and break clauses. NHSC operates on a **cost-recovery basis**, charging for technical draw-down days at fixed rates.
how_mechanism.q13_structure_description: The **NHSC acts as a central platform** coordinating technical expertise from UK health institutions (ALBs). FCDO provides oversight via a Strategic Advisory Board and Post-level commissioning. The NHSC triages requests, matches experts, and manages delivery, while FCDO Posts quality-assure interventions.
how_mechanism.q14_selection_rationale: The NHSC was selected as the **sole provider** due to its unique ability to leverage the NHS brand, access a broad range of UK health expertise, and build on its role in the predecessor Better Health Programme. Alternatives (e.g., open competition) were ruled out because no other entity could replicate the NHSC’s credibility or ecosystem access.

quote.instrument: "The NHSC operates on a cost-recovery process... the agreement will be governed by a non-legally binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)." (D0003600.odt, Commercial Case)
quote.selection: "The alternative – individual commissioning of technical expertise from each ALB – is deemed to be unwieldy and unmanageable... As such, a single-source approach is unlikely to face commercial challenge and is proposed." (D0003600.odt, Value for Money)

q17_governance_details.name: HealthSystemsConnect Programme Strategic Advisory Board (SAB)
composition: Chair: Health Systems Team Leader or Head of Human Development Department (FCDO)
Members: Senior reps from DHSC International, DBT, FCDO Health Diplomacy Lead, External Adviser (TBD)
Ad-hoc: FCDO Post reps for country-specific discussions
q17_governance_details.role: Provides strategic advice, challenges programme delivery, monitors NHSC’s wider footprint across FCDO network.

quote.governance: "The Board will meet first at the end of inception when they will provide expert challenge on year one plans and priorities, and then annually or on an exceptional basis as needed." (D0003600.odt, Management Case)
quote.oversight: "FCDO will undertake annual reviews to measure progress against outputs, outcomes and VfM... The annual review process will provide recommendations to enhance delivery on activities and milestones that are facing challenges or are slower to deliver." (D0003600.odt, Annual Reviews)

how_flexibility.q19_reallocation_details: Funds can be reallocated between the **intensive partnership** (5-6 priority countries) and **rapid-response window** (wider network) annually, based on demand and effectiveness. A ring-fenced budget (30 NHS ALB days) is reserved for rapid-response, but this can be reviewed.
how_flexibility.q20_adaptive_management_details: The programme uses a **3-month inception phase** to finalize country selection and work plans. Annual reviews allow adjustments based on demand, performance, and wider FCDO priorities. The Theory of Change and log frame are refined iteratively.

quote.flexibility: "The balance of costs between core NHSC (PMO and core technical function) and NHS ALB technical draw-down will be reviewed as part of ongoing financial management and through annual reviews." (D0003600.odt, Financial Details)
quote.adaptive: "Initial country selection will take place during a three-month inception period when more detailed work-plans will be established." (D0003600.odt, Appraisal Approach)

how_efficiency.q22_layers_description: FCDO → NHSC (platform) → NHS ALB technical experts (no further sub-awards)

quote.costs: "Central NHSC (PMO and core technical function) overheads (set at 11%)." (D0003600.odt, Budget Breakdown)
quote.payments: "In year one the lead host of the NHSC will be paid six-monthly in arrears following submission of a financial report indicating spend and updated forecast." (D0003600.odt, Financial Management)

q24_alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Would halt all central government-financed health partnership activity, losing opportunities for global health diplomacy and UHC progress.
NHSC’s unique positioning (NHS brand credibility + access to UK health ecosystem) made alternatives unviable.
Evidence supports country-led, demand-responsive approaches for effective partnerships.

q24_alternatives_considered.option: intensive investment in small set of countries (Option 1)
q24_alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Limited geographic reach; lower potential for cross-country learning.

q24_alternatives_considered.option: lighter-touch, demand-responsive offer to wider countries (Option 2)
q24_alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Lower control over risks/delivery; weaker partnerships and sustainability.

q24_alternatives_considered.rationale: Balances intensive support for 5-6 priority countries with a rapid-response window for wider influence.

why_rationale.q25_why_chosen: The **mixed model (Option 3)** was selected for its **value for money**, **flexibility**, and **alignment with FCDO’s strategic goals**. It combines deep partnerships in priority countries with agility to respond to unplanned opportunities, leveraging the NHSC’s unique access to UK health expertise while mitigating risks of overstretch or low impact.
q25_decision_factors: vfm (NHSC’s cost-recovery rates and efficiency gains)
risk-mitigation (balanced geographic spread and break clauses)
experience (builds on Better Health Programme lessons)
equity (focus on ODA-eligible countries and UHC goals)

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Demand outstrips NHSC/ALB technical capacity
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Develop core knowledge products to reduce reliance on draw-down; define country criteria to prioritize requests.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Rapid-response component delivers limited sustained impact
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Ring-fence budget for rapid-response (30 days); review effectiveness annually.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Over-reliance on NHS brand credibility (if domestic pressures arise)
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Break clauses in MoU; diversify NHSC’s client base to reduce FCDO dependency.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Duplication with other FCDO health programmes
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Central oversight of all NHSC activity via MoU; Strategic Advisory Board monitors footprint.

vfm_criteria_used: economy (low NHSC overheads at 11%; cost-recovery pricing)
efficiency (single platform reduces transaction costs; reusable knowledge products)
effectiveness (demand-responsive model; focus on UHC policy influence)
equity (ODA-eligible countries; GESI framework for inclusion)

quote.rationale: "The mixed model... includes a more intensive offer to a sub-set of countries complemented by a small rapid-response window to capitalise on unique and unpredictable opportunities to influence and support wider health diplomacy efforts." (D0003600.odt, Appraisal Approach)
quote.vfm: "Keydrivers of Value for Money (VfM) include: Economy (NHS technical experts charged at ~£500/day on cost-recovery basis)... Efficiency (NHSC delivery model reduces transaction costs)... Effectiveness (matching expertise to demand; leveraging wider investments)." (D0003600.odt, Value for Money)

intersections.q27_where_constrains_who: Partner selection is constrained by **ODA eligibility**, **country demand for UK expertise**, and **health system maturity** (must be able to engage in mutual partnerships). The NHSC’s technical capacity also limits the number of countries that can be supported intensively.
q27_constraints_detail: ODA eligibility (all partners must be ODA-eligible countries)
government-led demand (countries must demonstrate political will for HSS)
health system maturity (must be able to benefit from mutual partnership)
NHSC capacity (limited ALB technical days available)
intersections.q28_what_determines_how: The **demand-responsive, partnership-based approach** (WHAT) requires a **flexible platform structure** (HOW) with rapid matching of experts to country needs. The focus on **cross-country learning** (WHAT) necessitates a **centralized NHSC hub** (HOW) to coordinate knowledge exchange.

q28_linkages.mechanism: NHSC’s triage and draw-down system for rapid expert matching
Centralized NHSC platform to host multi-country exchanges
FCDO Post commissioning of assignments with NHSC quality assurance

intersections.q29_equity_vs_efficiency_tradeoffs: The programme explicitly balances **equity** (inclusive access to UK expertise for ODA-eligible countries) with **efficiency** (prioritizing countries with highest demand/maturity). The **GESI framework** ensures inclusion, while the **mixed model** optimizes reach vs. depth.

q29_tradeoffs_detail.detail: Intensive support for 5-6 countries (depth) vs. rapid-response window for wider network (breadth).
UK experts lead technical draw-down, but co-development and mutual learning are emphasized.
Ring-fenced rapid-response budget (30 days) limits ad-hoc support to manage costs.

intersections.risk_affects_management: The **moderate risk profile** drives **milestone-based oversight** (annual reviews, break clauses) and **flexible funding** (ability to scale up/down). High-reputation risks (e.g., NHS brand) trigger **contingency planning** (e.g., MoU break clauses).
intersections.capacity_shapes_roles: The **capacity building objective** (peer learning, delegation visits) shapes partner roles: NHSC acts as a **knowledge broker**, while partner countries **co-develop solutions** rather than passively receive assistance. Southern partners must have **sufficient technical capacity** to engage in mutual exchanges.

quote.constraints: "While country eligibility and selection criteria will be finalised during the inception period, it is likely that the country mix will include some continued activity building on growing partnerships in Better Health Programme countries (e.g. Philippines, South Africa) and/or new partnerships in FCDO ‘Ending Preventable Deaths (EPD) Flagship’ countries... where the health system is deemed mature enough to benefit from a mutual partnership approach." (D0003600.odt, Strategic Case)
quote.tradeoffs: "The programme will not operate as stand-alone interventions, but rather complement a wider set of health FCDO health influencing, investment and innovation activity... as part of a wider partnership to work in partnership with host countries to achieve universal health coverage by 2030." (D0003600.odt, Theory of Change)

key_programme_risks.risk: Changes in UK/partner government priorities reduce demand for NHS expertise
FCDO budget reductions force programme re-scoping
NHSC/ALB capacity unable to meet country demand
Rapid-response component fails to deliver sustained impact
Reputational damage from NHS domestic pressures
Safeguarding incident affects vulnerable populations
Duplication with other FCDO health programmes

risk_mitigation_pairs.mitigation: Flexible, demand-led design with ability to scale up/down; break clauses in MoU.
In-built ability to scale investment; early identification of ODA cuts to allow re-scoping.
Develop core knowledge products to reduce draw-down needs; define country criteria to prioritize requests.
Ring-fence 30 NHS ALB days for rapid-response; review effectiveness annually.
Monitor NHS domestic context; diversify NHSC client base to reduce FCDO dependency.
NHSC safeguarding policies cascaded to all deployed experts; whistleblowing mechanisms.
Central oversight of NHSC activity via MoU; Strategic Advisory Board monitors footprint.

fcas_specific_lessons: No explicit FCAS-specific lessons mentioned. The programme targets ODA-eligible countries but does not focus on fragile/conflict-affected states (FCAS) as a priority.
risks_lessons.lessons_from_previous:
Lessons from the **Better Health Programme** (predecessor) shaped the NHSC’s role, including: 
- Importance of **demand-responsive technical partnerships** over traditional aid dynamics.
- Value of **cross-country learning networks** for sustainability.
- Need for **flexible funding** to adapt to country needs.
- **Mutual benefit** approach (UK and partner countries both gain skills).
design_changes_based_on_learning: Added **rapid-response window** (30 days) to complement intensive country support.
Included **Strategic Advisory Board** for cross-FCDO coordination (lesson from Better Health’s siloed delivery).
Explicit **GESI framework** to address equity gaps identified in predecessor.
**Cost-recovery pricing** for NHSC to ensure sustainability post-FCDO funding.

quote.lessons: "The UK has a strong experience and reputation in health partnerships through its long history of DFID, DHSC and FCDO health partnerships programming, in particular the NHSC and the partnerships established in countries such as Thailand, the Philippines, South Africa and Brazil under the recent Better Health Programme." (D0003600.odt, Strategic Case)
quote.design_changes: "The programme is built upon the principles of mutual partnership and patient development and will complement wider UK health investments... learning from the Better Health Programme’s focus on higher-level system capabilities." (D0003600.odt, Strategic Case)

financial_details.leverage_achieved: The programme aims to **catalyze additional funding** (e.g., Malawi example where NHSC input led to Norwegian Institute of Public Health funding for a new public health cadre). However, no explicit co-funding targets are stated.

quote.budget: "The budget for this programme is up to £2.93m of ODA, RDEL over three years... NHSC (PMO and core technical function) overheads (set at 11%)." (D0003600.odt, Financial Details)
quote.leverage: "This work has, in turn, catalysed funding from the Norwegian Institute of Public Health to pilot and evaluate the training of a new public health cadre over the next two years." (D0003600.odt, Outcome 1 Example)

metadata.programme_name: The Climate and Health Programme – supporting UK’s leadership role on the climate and health agenda

quote.text: The Climate and Health Programme will help strengthen global efforts, reach and financing to improve the climate resilience of developing country health systems and reduce health system emissions.

metadata.duration_source: AMP Start Date: July 2023; AMP End Date: March 2027

what_objectives.q1_explanation: The programme combines capacity building (strengthening health systems' climate resilience), policy influence (through ATACH coordination), implementation research (testing interventions in 5 countries), and financing mechanisms (leveraging climate funds). It aims to reduce preventable deaths from climate impacts while making health systems low-carbon.
what_objectives.q1_source: The Climate and Health Programme will help strengthen global efforts, reach and financing to improve the climate resilience of developing country health systems and reduce health system emissions. It will do this through 1) strengthening international leadership and coordination through the Alliance for Transformative Action on Climate and Health (ATACH), 2) using targeted catalytic investments and expertise to support countries deliver on their commitments, and 3) helping countries to increase resource mobilisation and leverage larger scale international financial resources for climate and health outcomes, including from climate funds.

q3_expected_outputs.output: ATACH Secretariat operational and able to demonstrate impact, expand reach, monitor and report progress
Countries assess the resilience of their health system to climate-related shocks, with support from the UK
q3_expected_outputs.quantitative: up to 5 EPD Flagship countries

q3_expected_outputs.output: Countries measure health sector's GHG emissions and develop action plans
Countries have demonstrable increased access to finance for implementation of climate and health action, on mitigation and adaptation measures
Improved international cooperation and dialogue at the intersection of climate and health
Health systems more resilient to climate-sensitive disease and climate-related shocks
Health systems with reduced carbon emissions
Increased international investment in building climate resilient and low carbon health systems
Reduction in the number of preventable deaths from the health impacts of climate change

what_objectives.summary: The programme aims to build climate-resilient, low-carbon health systems in developing countries through global coordination (ATACH), country-level technical assistance, and leveraging international climate finance. It directly addresses the intersection of climate change and health, focusing on vulnerable populations and systemic transformation.

quote.text: This programme will help strengthen global efforts, by building capacity and helping to increase access to financing to improve the climate resilience of health systems and reduce health system emissions, particularly in developing countries.
quote.source: D0006007.odt, WHAT THE PROGRAMME SEEKS TO ACHIEVE

countries_regions: Global (with focus on up to 5 EPD Flagship countries: Bangladesh, DRC, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan)
where_context.q5_risk_evidence: The programme has a "moderate" residual risk rating, with risks including governments failing to prioritise climate and health, inadequate international finance, and potential fragmentation of efforts. The climate crisis itself could accelerate beyond adaptation capacities.
where_context.q5_source: The programme has a "moderate" residual risk rating.
q6_contextual_constraints: limited country capacity on climate and health
where_context.q6_constraints_impact: Weak health system resilience to climate shocks, limited technical expertise in LMICs on climate-health integration, and risks of overlapping efforts without coordination. Climate impacts (e.g., heatwaves, floods) directly strain health systems, while fragmented global responses may dilute impact.

quote.text: The health impacts of climate change can be direct (heat, flood, wildfire, storms, and drought), ecosystem-mediated (vector-borne diseases, food-and water-borne infections, air quality), or indirect through human or social responses to climate change (e.g., malnutrition, migration, and conflict).
quote.source: D0006007.odt, Evidence of need for action

who_partners.lead_institution_name: Alliance for Transformative Action on Climate and Health (ATACH)
who_partners.q9_north_south_decision_power: The UK (FCDO) and WHO co-convene ATACH, with decision-making power resting in the secretariat (WHO-hosted) and FCDO’s funding/strategic direction. Southern partners (LMIC governments) are recipients of technical assistance and funding but have limited influence over global coordination.
q10_capacity_building_details: technical assistance to countries for vulnerability assessments
GHG emissions baseline measurements
development of adaptation/mitigation plans
training for health professionals on climate literacy
support to multilateral organizations (e.g., World Bank, ADB) to integrate climate-health

partner_organizations.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
partner_organizations.role: ATACH secretariat host; global coordination

partner_organizations.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)
partner_organizations.role: funding; strategic leadership; co-convener of ATACH

partner_organizations.name: Asian Development Bank (ADB)
partner_organizations.role: potential Climate and Health Hub in India; financing mechanisms

partner_organizations.name: World Bank
partner_organizations.role: climate and health economic toolkits; investment case development

partner_organizations.name: Green Climate Fund (GCF)
partner_organizations.role: co-investment framework for climate and health

partner_organizations.name: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
partner_organizations.role: collaboration with GCF/WHO on investment frameworks

partner_organizations.name: Health Care Without Harm (HCWH)
partner_organizations.role: evidence generation; best practices

partner_organizations.name: Wellcome Trust
partner_organizations.role: research funding; evidence support

partner_organizations.name: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM)
partner_organizations.role: research; technical expertise

partner_organizations.name: EPD Flagship Countries (e.g., Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Kenya)
partner_organizations.role: recipients of bilateral technical assistance

quote.text: The UK is well placed to respond to these challenges, having played a leading role on climate and health due to the success of the COP26 health programme where diplomatic efforts led to over 50 nations committing to build climate-resilient and low-carbon sustainable health systems.
quote.source: D0006007.odt, Rationale for UK Aid spending

how_mechanism.q12_instrument_explanation: Core funding to WHO for ATACH secretariat (block funding); contracts/grants for bilateral technical assistance in 5 countries; potential contributions to multilateral initiatives (e.g., World Bank, ADB) via partnership agreements. The programme may also use FCDO secondees or programme-funded roles for short-term expertise.
how_mechanism.q13_structure_description: ATACH serves as the central coordination platform, with the UK (FCDO) and WHO as co-conveners. Bilateral activities in 5 countries are managed through FCDO country posts, while multilateral engagements (e.g., World Bank, ADB) are overseen via separate agreements. An internal FCDO board assesses country/multilateral proposals.
how_mechanism.q14_selection_rationale: ATACH was established post-COP26 based on country demand, with the UK and WHO as natural conveners. Bilateral country selection is based on EPD Flagship status and FCDO post advice, not open competition. Multilateral partners (e.g., World Bank, ADB) were chosen for their existing climate-health tools and global reach.

quote.text: The first phase of the programme will focus on strengthening international leadership and coordination on climate and health. Partners have already produced investible plans to deliver in these areas, meaning the activity can begin immediately.
quote.source: D0006007.odt, WHAT THE PROGRAMME WILL DO

how_governance.q17_governance_details: An internal FCDO board, led by the Deputy Director of Human Development Department and including the Head of Climate, Environment and Health Team, assesses country proposals and multilateral options. Decisions are made based on criteria like leverage potential, equity, and alignment with HMG objectives.

quote.text: To confirm specific programme investments under components 2-3 we will set up an internal board to assess the country proposals and multilateral programme options to decide on which to proceed with based on a set of criteria.

how_flexibility.q19_reallocation_details: The programme is designed with flexibility in Years 2+ to adapt to emerging opportunities, but reallocation between components requires internal board approval. Phase 2 activities will be assessed annually.
how_flexibility.q20_adaptive_management_details: The programme includes an adaptive approach to respond to new evidence, particularly in outer years. Adjustments require review by the internal board and are tied to annual milestones.

quote.text: The scope and level of resource devoted to each component will be flexible (particularly in year 2 and beyond), allowing the programme to adapt to emerging opportunities and risks.
quote.source: D0006007.odt, WHAT THE PROGRAMME WILL DO

how_efficiency.q22_layers_description: FCDO → ATACH/WHO (for global coordination); FCDO → Country Posts/Implementing Partners (for bilateral activities). Multilateral engagements add a third layer (FCDO → MDB/UN → country).

quote.text: Proposals will be assessed against the criteria set out in the Appraisal, Commercial and Management Case with a view to beginning activity in Year 2 (2024/25).

q24_alternatives_considered: Option 1: Do nothing (counterfactual)
Option 2: Support only ATACH (Component 1)
Option 3.1: ATACH-led technical assistance
Option 3.2: International organization (e.g., MDB)-led delivery
Option 3.3: Standalone Technical Assistance Fund for EPD countries
Option 3.4: Supplement existing FCDO country programmes
why_rationale.q25_why_chosen: Option 3 (mixed bilateral/multilateral delivery) was selected to balance UK leadership (via ATACH), direct country impact (through EPD Flagship support), and leverage of multilateral finance. The dual approach addresses both global coordination gaps and country-specific needs, while mitigating risks of fragmentation.
q25_decision_factors: risk mitigation (avoiding over-reliance on single partners)
partner capacity (building on WHO/ATACH’s convening power)

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Governments fail to prioritise climate and health, limiting impact of technical assistance.
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Engage FCDO country posts to align with national priorities and use political capital.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Fragmented efforts due to poor coordination among partners.
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: ATACH’s role as a global hub; FCDO-led board to oversee coherence.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Inadequate international finance for country plans.
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Focus on investment case development and leveraging climate funds (e.g., GCF).

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: ATACH loses relevance if a competing coordination body emerges.
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: UK political backing and annual reviews to adapt ATACH’s role.

quote.text: It is right to strengthen international action through supporting ATACH, as the only global platform supporting countries to implement their commitments to climate resilient and low carbon sustainable health systems. We must also support countries to deliver on their commitments now...

intersections.q27_where_constrains_who: The global scope and focus on LMICs constrain partner selection to organizations with multilateral reach (e.g., WHO, World Bank) or existing FCDO frameworks. Fragile contexts (e.g., South Sudan, Somalia) limit direct implementation to trusted partners with in-country presence.
q27_constraints_detail: Need for partners with existing LMIC operations (rules out newer actors)
Preference for multilateral organizations to ensure scale and legitimacy
FCAS contexts require partners with conflict sensitivity expertise
intersections.q28_what_determines_how: The mixed objectives (global coordination + country implementation) necessitate a dual structure: ATACH for policy influence and multilateral engagement, paired with bilateral technical assistance for direct impact. The need to leverage climate finance shapes the focus on investment cases and project pipelines.
q28_linkages: Global coordination (ATACH) → enables country-level technical assistance by providing tools/standards
Country diagnostics → feed into global evidence base (ATACH) and multilateral financing mechanisms
UK leadership role → justifies direct management of bilateral components
intersections.q29_equity_vs_efficiency_tradeoffs: The programme explicitly balances equity (targeting vulnerable countries/populations) with efficiency (leveraging multilaterals for scale). Trade-offs include: (1) focusing on 5 EPD countries for depth vs. broader reach, and (2) prioritizing ATACH’s global role over direct country spending.
q29_tradeoffs_detail: speed vs. inclusion: Rapid ATACH setup vs. slower country-level engagement
Northern expertise vs. Southern ownership: UK/WHO leadership in ATACH vs. LMIC-led implementation
cost vs. reach: Bilateral technical assistance (higher cost) vs. multilateral channels (broader impact)
intersections.risk_affects_management: The moderate risk profile drives milestone-based oversight (e.g., annual board reviews) and adaptive management, particularly for Phase 2 activities where uncertainties are higher.
intersections.capacity_shapes_roles: Capacity building is core to partner roles: ATACH partners (e.g., WHO, HCWH) provide global technical leadership, while country posts/implementers deliver context-specific support. Southern partners (LMIC governments) are positioned as recipients of capacity strengthening.

quote.text: The programme will therefore ensure coherence and increase the evidence base of successful interventions in building climate resilient and sustainable health systems through country level diagnostics and monitoring and evaluation of activities.
quote.source: D0006007.odt, WHAT THE PROGRAMME SEEKS TO ACHIEVE

key_programme_risks: Governments fail to prioritise climate and health, undermining technical assistance.
Posts fail to engage actively on the agenda, limiting country-level impact.
Stakeholders fail to collaborate, leading to fragmented efforts.
Inadequate international finance for country plans.
Emergence of competing coordination platforms to ATACH.
Climate crisis accelerates beyond adaptation capacities.
Overlap with other UK programmes (e.g., EPD) creating inefficiencies.

risk_mitigation_pairs.risk: Governments fail to prioritise climate and health
risk_mitigation_pairs.mitigation: Engage FCDO country posts to use political capital and align with national priorities.
Design bilateral support to complement existing health programmes, ensuring Post ownership.
ATACH’s coordination role; FCDO-led board to oversee coherence.
Focus on investment case development and leveraging climate funds (e.g., GCF, World Bank).
UK political backing and annual reviews to adapt ATACH’s mandate.
Adaptive programme design with flexibility in Years 2+.

fcas_specific_lessons: In FCAS contexts (e.g., Somalia, South Sudan), prioritise partners with existing in-country networks and conflict sensitivity.
Use FCDO country posts as intermediaries to navigate political/economic constraints.
risks_lessons.lessons_from_previous: The success of COP26 health commitments (50+ countries) demonstrated the value of high-level diplomacy paired with technical support. ATACH was created to address the post-COP26 gap in implementation coordination.
risks_lessons.design_changes_based_on_learning: Phase 2 was designed to be flexible based on Phase 1 lessons, with a focus on scaling successful country models and adapting to emerging multilateral opportunities (e.g., ADB’s Climate and Health Hub).

quote.text: The programme has a "moderate" residual risk rating. Key risks identified for the C&H programme include: Governments fail to prioritise climate and health...; The interventions identified by host countries are insufficient...; Posts fail to engage actively...

co_funding_partners.partner: Potential: Canada, Netherlands, Wellcome Trust, HCWH (for ATACH activities)

financial_details.leverage_achieved: The programme aims to leverage larger-scale international financial resources, including climate funds (e.g., GCF), multilateral development banks (World Bank, ADB), and global foundations. Specific leverage targets are not quantified but are a core objective.

quote.text: Programme Value: Up to £18m (RDEL, 100% ICF).

metadata.programme_name: Promoting Equalities Regional Programme (PEP-Regional)

quote.programme_name: "Promoting Equalities Regional Programme (PEP-Regional)" (D0003454.odt, Title)
quote.budget: "£4.9m over four years" (D0003454.odt, Programme summary)
quote.duration: "four years" (D0003454.odt, Programme summary)
quote.sector: "Gender and Equalities, global" (D0003454.odt, Metadata section)

metadata.duration_source: "£4.9m over four years will contribute to building a safer, more equitable and prosperous world" (D0003454.odt, Programme summary)

what_objectives.q1_explanation: PEP-Regional combines capacity building (strengthening FCDO's regional networks and capabilities), policy influence (driving national-level policy shifts on gender and equalities), and implementation support (through an Enabling Fund for targeted initiatives). The programme also includes a knowledge-sharing component (Gateway portal) to showcase UK expertise as a global public good.
what_objectives.q1_source: "PEP-Regional will strengthen regional networks and partnerships, enhancing effective use of positions of power and influence, increasing targeted policy action, empowering civil society organisations and supporting national level shifts in discourse towards gender and equalities issues." (D0003454.odt, Programme summary)

q3_expected_outputs.output: Regionally focused gender and equalities advisory resource (1-4 posts)
Enabling Fund for small strategic initiatives at national/regional levels
Gender and Equalities Gateway (external/internal portal for FCDO resources)
Strengthened regional networks and partnerships (e.g., MENAD Gender Equality Network)
National policy actions and ODA programming using UK expertise (e.g., gender charters, GESI analysis)
Capacity-building initiatives (training, workshops, awareness-raising)
Global public goods (events, research publications, evidence dissemination)

what_objectives.summary: PEP-Regional aims to build FCDO's capabilities to advance gender and equalities globally by embedding a focus on marginalized groups across diplomacy and development. It combines advisory support, strategic funding, and knowledge-sharing to drive policy change, empower civil society, and position the UK as a leader in this field.

quote.objectives: "The programme will deliver through three key components: [1] Regionally focused gender and equalities advisory resource... [2] An Enabling Fund accessible by posts... [3] A Gateway that serves as a portal for access to key FCDO resources..." (D0003454.odt, Programme summary)
quote.approach: "This regional programme is designed to increase the impact of FCDO’s work worldwide on advancing equality and tackling the barriers that cause discrimination and marginalisation... building capability across the FCDO and ensuring a globally coherent approach." (D0003454.odt, Context section)

where_context.q5_risk_evidence: The programme operates in fragile and conflict-affected states (FCAS) and countries with active terrorist organizations, but robust financial and safeguarding controls are implemented to manage risks. The overall risk rating is assessed as 'moderate' due to the programme's scale and ambition.
where_context.q5_source: "The overall risk rating for the delivery of the programme is ‘moderate’. This reflects the size, scale, and ambition of the programme, including working with small organisations. The programme team will work with delivery partners to develop more detailed risk registers for each workstream and individual projects." (D0003454.odt, Risk section)
where_context.q6_constraints_impact: Political rollbacks on women's and LGBT+ rights, limited ODA resources in regions like Latin America, and systemic discrimination against marginalized groups (e.g., people with disabilities, LGBT+ communities) create challenges for policy influence and programme delivery. Climate vulnerabilities and weak social protection systems further exacerbate inequalities.

quote.scope: "The programme will broadly work across four regions with the specific perimeters to be determined during the programme’s first six months. Indicatively these are: Latin America, Africa, MENA and Asia." (D0003454.odt, Approach section)
quote.risk: "The programme will work in a range of countries, including in fragile and conflict affected states and in countries where known terrorist organisations are operating." (D0003454.odt, Risk section)
quote.constraints: "Inequality undermines social justice and human rights... Excluding these groups has had substantial social, political, and economic costs... Advancing gender equality and standing up for women and girls’ rights are a core part of the UK Government’s mission and Global Britain’s role as a force for good in the world." (D0003454.odt, Context section)

who_partners.q9_north_south_decision_power: FCDO retains decision-making authority over programme design, funding allocation, and strategic priorities. Regional advisory roles and local posts implement activities but operate within FCDO's framework and oversight.
q10_capacity_building_details: training workshops
guidance dissemination
awareness-raising events
technical assistance for policy/programming
network-building (e.g., regional gender equality networks)
support to civil society organizations (CSOs) and rights movements

partner_organizations.name: FCDO regional posts (e.g., MENAD, East Africa, Latin America)
partner_organizations.role: Implementation of national/regional activities; policy influence; local partnership management

partner_organizations.name: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), including women's rights organizations (WROs) and LGBT+ rights groups
partner_organizations.role: Advocacy; local programme delivery; policy shaping

partner_organizations.role: Technical collaboration; global advocacy

partner_organizations.name: Academic/research institutions
partner_organizations.role: Evidence generation; GESI analysis

partner_organizations.role: Technical advisory support; capacity building

partner_organizations.name: Disability Inclusion Helpdesk / Centres of Expertise (COEs)
partner_organizations.role: Specialized technical assistance

quote.structure: "The programme will strengthen bridges between central teams, regions, and posts, enabling better sharing of resources, evidence and expertise on equalities..." (D0003454.odt, Approach section)
quote.capacity_building: "Component 1: regionally focused gender and equalities advisory resource to provide practical and evidence-based policy and advisory support... Component 2: an Enabling Fund accessible by posts to support targeted initiatives... Component 3: a Gender and Equalities Gateway..." (D0003454.odt, Programme components)
quote.partners: "Convening local civil society, human rights defenders, LGBT+ rights organisations and women’s rights organisations, networks and allies to support and shape policy development." (D0003454.odt, Enabling Fund section)

how_mechanism.q12_instrument_explanation: The programme uses a combination of **core FCDO funding** for advisory roles and the Gateway, and an **Enabling Fund** (likely grant-based) for small, strategic initiatives at the national/regional level. The business case explicitly appraises options including fully in-house delivery or outsourced via Accountable Grant.
how_mechanism.q13_structure_description: FCDO acts as the fund manager, overseeing regional advisory roles and the Enabling Fund. Regional advisers (FCDO staff or seconded experts) work closely with posts to identify priorities and allocate Enabling Fund resources. The Gateway is centrally managed but draws on decentralized inputs.

quote.instrument: "Option 1: Fully in-house; Option 2: Fully outsourced through an Accountable Grant" (D0003454.odt, Summary of Options)
quote.structure: "PEP-Regional will fund additional gender and equalities advisory roles to support the scale up of FCDO’s ambition... The Enabling Fund will provide modest, targeted funding to posts to take forward strategic activities... The Gateway... will facilitate easy access to high-quality FCDO technical resources." (D0003454.odt, Components 1-3)

how_governance.q16_sub_award_details: Regional advisory roles work with posts to identify Enabling Fund opportunities, but final allocation likely requires FCDO approval (e.g., alignment with Women and Girls Strategy).

quote.management: "The programme management team will review the programme’s level of risk at quarterly programme management meetings." (D0003454.odt, Risk section)
quote.sub_awards: "Regional roles will work with posts and regional offers on effective use of the funding..." (D0003454.odt, Enabling Fund section)

how_flexibility.q19_reallocation_details: Flexibility is built into the Enabling Fund to scale up proven approaches, but reallocation between major components (e.g., advisory roles vs. Gateway) likely requires approval.
how_flexibility.q20_adaptive_management_details: The programme is designed to adapt based on ongoing monitoring and learning, particularly in the first six months (e.g., refining regional perimeters). The Theory of Change assumes flexibility to respond to political contexts and emerging opportunities.

quote.flexibility: "Flexibility will be built in to potentially allow scale up of some approaches where these are proven to be effective." (D0003454.odt, Enabling Fund section)
quote.adaptive: "The programme is designed to be flexible so that the overall approach and each component can be adapted based on learnings from ongoing monitoring." (D0003454.odt, Theory of Change)

how_efficiency.q22_layers_description: FCDO → (1) Regional advisory roles/Enabling Fund managers → (2) Local posts/CSO partners.

quote.layers: "Regionally focused gender and equalities advisory resource to provide practical and evidence-based policy and advisory support on FCDO’s gender and equalities strategic priorities to regional networks... An Enabling Fund accessible by posts to support targeted initiatives..." (D0003454.odt, Components 1-2)
quote.payment: "Robust financial management will be implemented throughout the delivery chain to mitigate potential risks." (D0003454.odt, Risk section)

q24_alternatives_considered: Option 1: Fully in-house delivery
Option 2: Fully outsourced through an Accountable Grant
why_rationale.q25_why_chosen: The mixed model (regional advisory roles + Enabling Fund + Gateway) was selected to **balance FCDO control with local flexibility**. In-house advisory roles ensure alignment with FCDO priorities, while the Enabling Fund allows posts to respond to context-specific opportunities. The Gateway leverages existing FCDO resources efficiently. This approach addresses capability gaps identified in the IDS and aligns with the UK’s ambition to scale up its global leadership on gender and equalities.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Fiduciary risks (e.g., funds diverted in fragile states)
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Robust financial management, due diligence assessments, and compliance monitoring throughout the delivery chain.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Delivery risks (e.g., working with small organizations in high-risk contexts)
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Quarterly risk reviews, tailored risk registers for each workstream, and escalation procedures.

q26_modality_specific_risks.risk: Safeguarding risks (e.g., sexual exploitation/abuse in partner organizations)
q26_modality_specific_risks.mitigation: Enhanced due diligence for partners, strict checks for grantees interacting with vulnerable groups, and alignment with FCDO’s safeguarding strategy.

quote.alternatives: "The three appraisal options have been measured against the counterfactual of not allocating funding to the PEP-Regional Programme." (D0003454.odt, Summary of Options)
quote.rationale: "This programme is designed to strengthen capabilities, build better understanding of national contexts and develop a more coherent approach to gender and equalities across the FCDO... The design of PEP-Regional responds to the issues set out in the Strategic Case, including growing inequalities and rollback in the rights of women and marginalised groups." (D0003454.odt, Theory of Change)
quote.risks: "Major risks to the programme include fiduciary, delivery and safeguarding risks... Separate risk management procedures will be agreed with each delivery partner." (D0003454.odt, Risk section)

intersections.q27_where_constrains_who: The regional scope and FCAS contexts limit partner selection to organizations with **local contextual knowledge, language skills, and resilience to political pressures**. For example, in Latin America, limited ODA resources require leveraging non-funded networks (e.g., informal gender equality groups across embassies). In MENA, the adviser’s role demands political astuteness to navigate sensitive issues like LGBT+ rights.
q27_constraints_detail: Political sensitivity (e.g., criminalization of LGBT+ relationships in 70 jurisdictions)
Limited ODA in regions like Latin America → reliance on low/no-cost collaboration
Fragility/conflict → need for partners with safeguarding capacity
Language/regional expertise → preference for embedded or local advisors
intersections.q28_what_determines_how: The **mixed objectives** (capacity building + policy influence + implementation) require a **multi-component structure**: advisory roles for technical support, the Enabling Fund for local flexibility, and the Gateway for global knowledge-sharing. The need to influence both **internal FCDO capabilities** and **external policy environments** drives the combination of centralized oversight (Gateway) and decentralized funding (Enabling Fund).
q28_linkages: Policy influence objective → regional advisory roles embedded in FCDO networks
Implementation support → Enabling Fund for context-specific initiatives
Knowledge-sharing → Gateway as a global public good
Capacity building → all components include training/mentorship elements
intersections.q29_equity_vs_efficiency_tradeoffs: Explicit tensions are noted between **scaling up quickly** (e.g., using existing FCDO cadres) and **ensuring local ownership** (e.g., supporting small CSOs with limited capacity). The Enabling Fund’s modest, targeted grants aim to balance efficiency with equity by funding high-impact, low-cost initiatives (e.g., Ambassador for a Day campaigns) while mitigating fiduciary risks.
q29_tradeoffs_detail: Speed vs. inclusion: "Demand from posts for resources, expertise, evidence and advice on gender and equalities issues is growing" (D0003454.odt, Capacity Building) vs. need to build capabilities in marginalized groups.
Expertise vs. ownership: Reliance on FCDO’s Social Development Cadre (Northern expertise) vs. goal of empowering local women’s/LGBT+/disability rights movements.
Cost vs. reach: Limited ODA in regions like Latin America requires "impactful activity at low or no cost" (D0003454.odt, Case Study 4).
intersections.risk_affects_management: The **moderate risk rating** (due to FCAS contexts and small-organization partners) justifies **quarterly oversight reviews** and **detailed risk registers per workstream**. For example, safeguarding risks in fragile states necessitate embedded advisors for Enabling Fund grantees.
intersections.capacity_shapes_roles: Capacity-building objectives shape partner roles by: (1) **Embedding advisory support** in FCDO posts to strengthen internal skills (e.g., GESI analysis); (2) **Funding CSO organizational strengthening** through the Enabling Fund; (3) **Designing the Gateway** as a learning tool for both FCDO staff and external partners.

quote.context_who: "LATAM posts... are supported by 50% of a regional gender officer based in BE Mexico City. This role supports posts to align activity with FCDO equalities priorities... A small amount of ODA funds in a region with limited programming can be highly strategic." (D0003454.odt, Case Study 4)
quote.what_how: "The programme will work through three key components... Regionally focused gender and equality advisory support... Enabling Fund accessible to posts... Gateway for gender and equalities resources." (D0003454.odt, Theory of Change)
quote.equity_efficiency: "The Enabling Fund will provide modest, targeted funding to posts to take forward strategic activities with the potential to advance equality and reduce discrimination at national or regional levels." (D0003454.odt, Component 2)
quote.risk_management: "The programme will work in a range of countries, including in fragile and conflict affected states... Robust financial management will be implemented throughout the delivery chain to mitigate potential risks." (D0003454.odt, Risk section)

key_programme_risks: Fiduciary risks (diversion of funds in FCAS contexts)
Delivery risks (working with small organizations with limited capacity)
Safeguarding risks (sexual exploitation/abuse in partner organizations)
Political risks (rollback on women’s/LGBT+ rights; perception of interference)
Coherence risks (ensuring alignment across FCDO’s regional and central teams)
Sustainability risks (maintaining progress post-programme)

risk_mitigation_pairs.mitigation: Due diligence assessments for all partners, compliance monitoring, and use of standard grant agreements with terrorism financing clauses.
Quarterly programme management reviews, tailored risk registers, and capacity-building support for grantees.
Enhanced due diligence, strict checks for grantees interacting with vulnerable groups, and alignment with FCDO’s safeguarding strategy.
Leveraging FCDO’s diplomatic networks and multilateral fora to advocate discreetly; adaptive programming to respond to changing contexts.
Regional advisory roles to bridge central teams and posts; shared workplans and charters (e.g., MENAD Gender Charter).

fcas_specific_lessons: Embedded, longer-term advisory roles are more effective in FCAS (e.g., MENAD Gender Adviser based in Abu Dhabi).
Small, strategic ODA funds can catalyze change in low-resource settings (e.g., Latin America’s Ambassador for a Day campaign).
Local contextual knowledge is critical for safeguarding and political navigation (e.g., LGBT+ rights in criminalized jurisdictions).
Regional networks reduce burden on smaller posts (e.g., 50% regional gender officer supporting Central America).

lessons_from_previous.technical_assistance: Longer-term, embedded advisers (e.g., Disability Inclusive Development secondees) are more effective than short-term experts. Success depends on building trust, aligning with local priorities, and brokering agreements.
lessons_from_previous.funding_models: Small, flexible funds (e.g., Magna Carta Fund) demonstrate that modest ODA can achieve strategic impact when paired with local contextual knowledge.
lessons_from_previous.networks: Informal networks (e.g., Latin America gender equality network) maximize collaboration at low cost but require dedicated coordination (e.g., regional gender officer role).
lessons_from_previous.capacity_building: Secondments (e.g., Sightsavers staff into FCDO) catalyze institutional change by combining technical input with internal advocacy.

design_changes_based_on_learning: Incorporated **regional advisory roles** based on evidence from MENAD and East Africa models, which showed the value of politically astute, networked advisers.
Designed the **Enabling Fund** to be flexible and modest, reflecting lessons from the Magna Carta Fund and COVID-19 SPACE helpline.
Added **Gateway component** to address gaps in visibility/access to FCDO’s existing resources (e.g., Helpdesks, COEs).
Emphasized **sustainability** by focusing on embedding capabilities within FCDO (e.g., training, GESI analysis) rather than standalone projects.

quote.risks: "Major risks to the programme include fiduciary, delivery and safeguarding risks... The programme team will work with delivery partners to develop more detailed risk registers for each workstream and individual projects." (D0003454.odt, Risk section)
quote.lessons: "Lessons from current regional approaches show innovative and effective models to building awareness and engagement... Longer term, embedded and programme funded advisers working alongside in-country posts can be most effective." (D0003454.odt, Current Approach section)
quote.design_changes: "This programme will align closely with recommendations and approaches within technical cadres and through FCDO’s International Academy... The programme is designed to be flexible so that the overall approach and each component can be adapted based on learnings." (D0003454.odt, Theory of Change)
